context: Request: the longest-running matter still open (not shelved; matters winding down in closing posture count as open) and its opening date, for an aging review. Rubric: 1044-00006 (Thalassa Shipping charter-party breach defense, opened October 16, 2023) as the answer, its precision, and the opening date. Runs answered 1026-00004 (deal closed June 2023), 1005-00004 (effectively dormant, closure recommended) and 1001-00005 (dormant).

runs.failure_point: It counted a matter classified dormant after its deal lapsed as open, and did not weigh the newer matter that qualifies although it had read one of its reports.

first_error.why: The answer counts as open a matter that its own reads (evidence seen at [70]-[160]) show was classified dormant after its deal lapsed, although the request excludes shelved matters.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [126] said dormant is neither clearly open nor shelved and the write review at [168] said the proposed deal may sit outside the open scope; the check stage re-read the dormancy memo and only added a qualification, keeping the matter.

other_errors.why: A later-opened matter whose litigation outcome report it read at [129]-[134] is not weighed as a candidate; the answer mentions only its sibling.
other_errors.critic_note: The review at [126] asked it to open this matter, which it did; no later review named how it was set aside.

divergence: All three fail the same way, at the write stage: each run ranked candidates by the oldest opening dates its scans and listings showed, screened older matters one batch at a time, and wrote an old matter that its own reads showed closed (T0) or dormant (T1, T2) as still open (over-inclusion). The matter that qualifies, opened later, appeared in folder lists and scan tables; only T2 opened it (one report) and did not weigh it. Reviews in T1 and T2 named the chosen matter's dormant status as doubtful and the agents only reworded; T0's reviews asked about coverage, never about the chosen matter's closed deal. The agent-declared new stages (store-wide date surveys and repeated verification passes in all runs) widened screening of older matters but did not change the ranking approach.
